patch_description: The current single-start winner is selected by the hard-min value after a fixed refine budget, then returned. The hard-min metric is notoriously plateau-prone: the winning start may just be lucky, and the runner-ups (often within a few percent) are discarded. I propose keeping the top-3 candidates from the multi-start loop and running an additional greedy, strictly-improving hard-min polish (with step-halving) on each of them before selecting the final winner. This is deterministic, cheap (~60 sweeps × 3 candidates), and directly attacks the hard-min objective with coordinate moves after the soft/hard search phases. I also tighten the hard-refine rounds slightly for better convergence per candidate. This follows the proven clip-then-renormalize projection (via _project_inside) and keeps the module-level caching for fast eval_time.
